claim: Plasma cells (PCs) are essential for protection from infection.
source: Plasma cells (PCs) are essential for protection from infection, and at the origin of incurable cancers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about plasma cells.

claim: Plasma cells are at the origin of incurable cancers.
source: Plasma cells (PCs) are essential for protection from infection, and at the origin of incurable cancers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about plasma cells.

claim: Current studies do not circumvent the limitations of removing PCs from their microenvironment and confound formation and maintenance.
source: Current studies do not circumvent the limitations of removing PCs from their microenvironment and confound formation and maintenance.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of current methodologies stated in the abstract.

claim: The investigation of PC population dynamics has mostly relied on nucleotide analog incorporation that does not label quiescent cells.
source: Also, the investigation of PC population dynamics has mostly relied on nucleotide analog incorporation that does not label quiescent cells, a property of most PCs.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current methodologies in the abstract.

claim: Most PCs are quiescent cells.
source: Also, the investigation of PC population dynamics has mostly relied on nucleotide analog incorporation that does not label quiescent cells, a property of most PCs.
evidence: This is stated as a known property of plasma cells in the abstract.

claim: The main impediment to studying PCs is the lack of tools to perform specific genetic manipulation in vivo.
source: The main impediment is the lack of tools to perform specific genetic manipulation in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as the primary limitation in the abstract.

claim: The JchaincreERT2 genetic tool permits first-ever specific genetic manipulation in PCs in vivo, across immunoglobulin isotypes.
source: Here we characterize a genetic tool (JchaincreERT2) in the mouse that permits first-ever specific genetic manipulation in PCs in vivo, across immunoglobulin isotypes.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Splenic and bone marrow PC numbers remained constant over-time.
source: Using this tool, we found that splenic and bone marrow PC numbers remained constant over-time with the decay in genetically labeled PCs being compensated by unlabeled PCs, supporting homeostatic population turnover in these tissues.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study stated in the abstract.

claim: The decay in genetically labeled PCs is compensated by unlabeled PCs in spleen and bone marrow.
source: Using this tool, we found that splenic and bone marrow PC numbers remained constant over-time with the decay in genetically labeled PCs being compensated by unlabeled PCs, supporting homeostatic population turnover in these tissues.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study stated in the abstract.

claim: Homeostatic population turnover occurs in splenic and bone marrow PC tissues.
source: Using this tool, we found that splenic and bone marrow PC numbers remained constant over-time with the decay in genetically labeled PCs being compensated by unlabeled PCs, supporting homeostatic population turnover in these tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data stated in the abstract.

claim: Antibodies produced by plasma cells are crucial for immune protection against infection.
source: Antibodies produced by plasma cells (PCs) are crucial for immune protection against infection and for vaccination success (Nutt et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Antibodies produced by plasma cells are crucial for vaccination success.
source: Antibodies produced by plasma cells (PCs) are crucial for immune protection against infection and for vaccination success (Nutt et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Upon activation, B cells terminally differentiate into PCs.
source: Upon activation, B cells terminally differentiate into PCs, a process initiated by the downregulation of the B cell transcription factor PAX5 (Kallies et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: B cell to PC differentiation is initiated by the downregulation of the B cell transcription factor PAX5.
source: Upon activation, B cells terminally differentiate into PCs, a process initiated by the downregulation of the B cell transcription factor PAX5 (Kallies et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: PAX5 downregulation allows the expression of multiple factors normally repressed by PAX5, including Xbp1 and Jchain.
source: This event allows the expression of multiple factors normally repressed by PAX5, including Xbp1 and Jchain (Castro and Flajnik, 2014; Nutt et al., 2015; Rinkenberger et al., 1996; Shaffer et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: PAX5 downregulation is followed by the expression of the transcription factors IRF4 and BLIMP1.
source: PAX5 downregulation is also followed by the expression of the transcription factors IRF4 and BLIMP1 that play essential roles in the establishment of the PC program (Kallies et al., 2007; Klein et al., 2006; Sciammas et al., 2006; Shapiro-Shelef et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: IRF4 and BLIMP1 play essential roles in the establishment of the PC program.
source: PAX5 downregulation is also followed by the expression of the transcription factors IRF4 and BLIMP1 that play essential roles in the establishment of the PC program (Kallies et al., 2007; Klein et al., 2006; Sciammas et al., 2006; Shapiro-Shelef et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Multiple myeloma is the second most frequent hematological malignancy overall.
source: Beyond physiology, multiple cancers have a PC as cell of origin, including multiple myeloma, the second most frequent hematological malignancy overall, and for which a cure remains to be found (Palumbo and Anderson, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: A cure for multiple myeloma remains to be found.
source: Beyond physiology, multiple cancers have a PC as cell of origin, including multiple myeloma, the second most frequent hematological malignancy overall, and for which a cure remains to be found (Palumbo and Anderson, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Most PC studies make use of in vitro and cell transfer systems that remove PCs from their microenvironment.
source: However, at least in part because of technical limitations most PC studies make use of in vitro and cell transfer systems that remove PCs from their microenvironment.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current methodologies.

claim: Current genetic manipulation of PCs is not specific and targets other cell populations such as B cells.
source: Currently, genetic manipulation of PCs is not specific and targets other cell populations such as B cells, confounding PC formation, and maintenance.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current methodologies.

claim: Jchain (Igj) had the highest level and most specific expression in PC populations among well-known PC-associated genes.
source: We found amongst well-known PC-associated genes, that Jchain (Igj) had the highest level and most specific expression in PC populations.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on gene expression analysis.

claim: JCHAIN is a small polypeptide required to multimerize IgM and IgA.
source: JCHAIN is a small polypeptide required to multimerize IgM and IgA, and necessary for the transport of these Ig classes across the mucosal epithelium in a poly-Ig receptor-mediated process (Brandtzaeg and Prydz, 1984; Castro and Flajnik, 2014; Max and Korsmeyer, 1985).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: JCHAIN is necessary for the transport of IgM and IgA across the mucosal epithelium in a poly-Ig receptor-mediated process.
source: JCHAIN is a small polypeptide required to multimerize IgM and IgA, and necessary for the transport of these Ig classes across the mucosal epithelium in a poly-Ig receptor-mediated process (Brandtzaeg and Prydz, 1984; Castro and Flajnik, 2014; Max and Korsmeyer, 1985).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: GFP as a reporter of Jchain expression occurred in PCs across immunoglobulin isotypes, including IgG1.
source: We found at the single cell level that GFP as a reporter of Jchain expression occurred in PCs across immunoglobulin isotypes, including IgG1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on single cell analysis.

claim: The JchaincreERT2 allele allowed inclusive genetic timestamping of PCs, independently of their cell cycle status.
source: This system allowed inclusive genetic timestamping of PCs, independently of their cell cycle status.
evidence: This is a finding from the study demonstrating the capability of the tool.

claim: Xbp1 was primarily expressed in PCs, but the expression in bone marrow PCs was less than two-fold greater than that of non-PC populations.
source: Xbp1 and Irf4 were primarily expressed in PCs, however, the expression in bone marrow PCs (B_PC_BM) was less than two-fold greater than that of non-PC populations (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Irf4 was primarily expressed in PCs, but the expression in bone marrow PCs was less than two-fold greater than that of non-PC populations.
source: Xbp1 and Irf4 were primarily expressed in PCs, however, the expression in bone marrow PCs (B_PC_BM) was less than two-fold greater than that of non-PC populations (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The expression of Sdc1 and Prdm1 was not specific to PCs.
source: The expression of Sdc1 and Prdm1 was not specific to PCs (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Peritoneal cavity macrophages expressed more Sdc1 than bone marrow PCs.
source: Notably, peritoneal cavity macrophages (MF_226+II+480lo_PC) expressed more Sdc1 than bone marrow PCs (B_PC_BM), and a subset of FOXP3+ T cells (Treg_4_FP3+_Nrplo_Co) expressed higher levels of Prdm1 than that observed in splenic plasmablasts (B_PB_Sp) and bone marrow PCs (B_PC_BM; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A subset of FOXP3+ T cells expressed higher levels of Prdm1 than that observed in splenic plasmablasts and bone marrow PCs.
source: Notably, peritoneal cavity macrophages (MF_226+II+480lo_PC) expressed more Sdc1 than bone marrow PCs (B_PC_BM), and a subset of FOXP3+ T cells (Treg_4_FP3+_Nrplo_Co) expressed higher levels of Prdm1 than that observed in splenic plasmablasts (B_PB_Sp) and bone marrow PCs (B_PC_BM; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Jchain had a forty-fold enrichment over germinal center B cells.
source: By contrast, Jchain had the highest level of transcript expression in PCs compared to non-PCs and was the most PC specific amongst all factors, with a forty-fold enrichment over germinal center (GC) B cells (B_GC_CB_Sp; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: B220 is expressed on the surface of B cells and downregulated during PC differentiation.
source: B220 is expressed on the surface of B cells and downregulated during PC differentiation (Pracht et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The fraction of CD138+ cells increased in populations with higher GFP expression and lower B220 expression.
source: Next, we determined the fraction of cells within these populations that expressed surface CD138, a commonly used marker to define PCs by flow-cytometry (Pracht et al., 2017). The GFPnegB220neg population did not contain CD138+ cells, however, the fraction of CD138+ cells increased in the remaining populations in agreement with the reduction of B220 expression during PC differentiation, and the GFPintB220int and GFPhighB220low populations were mostly composed of CD138+ cells (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The GFPintB220int and GFPhighB220low populations were mostly composed of CD138+ cells.
source: The GFPnegB220neg population did not contain CD138+ cells, however, the fraction of CD138+ cells increased in the remaining populations in agreement with the reduction of B220 expression during PC differentiation, and the GFPintB220int and GFPhighB220low populations were mostly composed of CD138+ cells (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: CXCR4 is a chemokine receptor that facilitates homing of PCs to the bone marrow.
source: Identical results were found when defining PCs using in addition surface expression of CXCR4, a chemokine receptor that facilitates homing of PCs to the bone marrow (Figure 2D,E; Hargreaves et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: Increased GFP expression from the JchaincreERT2 allele associates with the loss of B220 and increased expression of PC-associated surface markers.
source: Thus, increased GFP expression from the JchaincreERT2 allele associates with the loss of B220 and increased expression of PC-associated surface markers.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the flow cytometry data.

claim: Virtually all CD138neg cells within the GFPlowB220high population of mice with the JchaincreERT2 allele expressed the B cell marker CD19.
source: Also above background, we found that virtually all CD138neg cells within the GFPlowB220high population of mice with the JchaincreERT2 allele expressed the B cell marker CD19 (Figure 2F), and in agreement with Jchain gene expression analysis (Figure 1D) these cells mostly represented germinal center (GC) B cells (CD38lowFAShigh; Figure 2F,G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: CD138neg cells within the GFPlowB220high population mostly represented germinal center (GC) B cells.
source: Also above background, we found that virtually all CD138neg cells within the GFPlowB220high population of mice with the JchaincreERT2 allele expressed the B cell marker CD19 (Figure 2F), and in agreement with Jchain gene expression analysis (Figure 1D) these cells mostly represented germinal center (GC) B cells (CD38lowFAShigh; Figure 2F,G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: Most PCs in the spleen and bone marrow expressed GFP (CD138+CXCR4+, 60 to 90%).
source: We found that most PCs in the spleen and bone marrow expressed GFP (CD138+CXCR4+, 60 to 90%; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: A minor fraction of B1b cells (0 to 6%) in the spleen expressed GFP.
source: We also observed that a minor fraction of B1b cells (0 to 6%) in the spleen expressed GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), possibly in agreement with the knowledge that B1b cells are prone to differentiate into PCs and are a source of IgM antibodies during T cell independent responses (Alugupalli et al., 2004).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: B1b cells are prone to differentiate into PCs and are a source of IgM antibodies during T cell independent responses.
source: We also observed that a minor fraction of B1b cells (0 to 6%) in the spleen expressed GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), possibly in agreement with the knowledge that B1b cells are prone to differentiate into PCs and are a source of IgM antibodies during T cell independent responses (Alugupalli et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The GFPnegB220neg population was virtually devoid of cells with BLIMP1 and IRF4 expression.
source: The GFPnegB220neg population was virtually devoid of cells with BLIMP1 and IRF4 expression (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Most GFPlowB220high cells were negative for BLIMP1 and IRF4.
source: However, most GFPlowB220high cells were negative for BLIMP1 and IRF4, suggesting that Jchain expression precedes that of IRF4 and BLIMP1, as previously observed in in vitro cultures of Blimp1 deficient B cells (Kallies et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis and comparison to previous work.

claim: Jchain expression precedes that of IRF4 and BLIMP1.
source: However, most GFPlowB220high cells were negative for BLIMP1 and IRF4, suggesting that Jchain expression precedes that of IRF4 and BLIMP1, as previously observed in in vitro cultures of Blimp1 deficient B cells (Kallies et al., 2007).
evidence: This is inferred from the data and supported by previous work.

claim: The vast majority of cells within the GFPintB220int and GFPhighB220low populations were BLIMP1+IRF4+.
source: Still, Jchain expression as measured by GFP strongly correlated with that of IRF4 and BLIMP1 given that the vast majority of cells within the GFPintB220int and GFPhighB220low populations were BLIMP1+IRF4+ (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: An in vivo population of cells exists in which Jchain expression preceded that of IRF4 and BLIMP1, possibly representing PC precursors.
source: Overall, we identified an in vivo population of cells in which Jchain expression preceded that of IRF4 and BLIMP1, possibly representing PC precursors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: GFP expression was highly enriched in plasmablasts compared to B cells in vitro.
source: GFP expression was highly enriched in plasmablasts compared to B cells and RFP expression was only observed upon addition of 4-OH tamoxifen to the cell culture, and that occurred virtually only in plasmablasts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on in vitro cell culture experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: RFP expression was only observed upon addition of 4-OH tamoxifen to the cell culture, and that occurred virtually only in plasmablasts.
source: GFP expression was highly enriched in plasmablasts compared to B cells and RFP expression was only observed upon addition of 4-OH tamoxifen to the cell culture, and that occurred virtually only in plasmablasts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on in vitro cell culture experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: creERT2 was specifically expressed by plasmablasts and effectively retained in the cytoplasm in the absence of 4-OH tamoxifen.
source: This data suggested that creERT2 was specifically expressed by plasmablasts and effectively retained in the cytoplasm in the absence of 4-OH tamoxifen.
evidence: This is inferred from the in vitro experimental data.

claim: In the absence of tamoxifen administration RFP expressing cells were not detected in vivo.
source: In the absence of tamoxifen administration RFP expressing cells were not detected, confirming the in vitro results and supporting that the JchaincreERT2 allele was not 'leaky' in the control of cre activity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on in vivo experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The JchaincreERT2 allele was not 'leaky' in the control of cre activity.
source: In the absence of tamoxifen administration RFP expressing cells were not detected, confirming the in vitro results and supporting that the JchaincreERT2 allele was not 'leaky' in the control of cre activity (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the in vivo experimental data.

claim: A small fraction of GFPlowB220high cells were positive for RFP in the spleen (median ~2%) and in the bone marrow (median ~1.2%).
source: Analyses of the populations defined by varied GFP and B220 surface expression (Figures 2 and 4B) revealed that a small fraction of GFPlowB220high cells were positive for RFP in the spleen (median ~2%) and in the bone marrow (median ~1.2%; Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Cre mediated recombination occurred in ~37% and~31% of GFPintB220int in the spleen and bone marrow, respectively.
source: In contrast, cre mediated recombination and as consequence RFP expression occurred in ~37% and~31% of GFPintB220int in the spleen and bone marrow, respectively, and the vast majority of cells within the GFPhighB220low population had undergone cre mediated recombination and were RFP positive (~76% in the spleen, and ~88% in the bone marrow, median; Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: The vast majority of cells within the GFPhighB220low population had undergone cre mediated recombination and were RFP positive (~76% in the spleen, and ~88% in the bone marrow, median).
source: In contrast, cre mediated recombination and as consequence RFP expression occurred in ~37% and~31% of GFPintB220int in the spleen and bone marrow, respectively, and the vast majority of cells within the GFPhighB220low population had undergone cre mediated recombination and were RFP positive (~76% in the spleen, and ~88% in the bone marrow, median; Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: JchaincreERT2 mediated cre-recombination was only effective in PC populations.
source: These data showed that JchaincreERT2 mediated cre-recombination was only effective in PC populations validating it as a tool to specifically perform genetic manipulation of PCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: IgG1 does not multimerize.
source: IgG1 does not multimerize, and due to differences in its secretory tail to that of IgA and IgM, JCHAIN does not associate with IgG1 (Johansen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: JCHAIN does not associate with IgG1 due to differences in its secretory tail to that of IgA and IgM.
source: IgG1 does not multimerize, and due to differences in its secretory tail to that of IgA and IgM, JCHAIN does not associate with IgG1 (Johansen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: It is currently suggested that Jchain expression occurs in all PCs regardless of isotype.
source: Currently it is suggested that Jchain expression occurs in all PCs regardless of isotype (Castro and Flajnik, 2014; Johansen et al., 2000; Mather et al., 1981).
evidence: This is stated as current understanding with citations.

claim: Jchain expression at the single cell level across immunoglobulin isotypes has not been demonstrated prior to this study.
source: Currently it is suggested that Jchain expression occurs in all PCs regardless of isotype (Castro and Flajnik, 2014; Johansen et al., 2000; Mather et al., 1981). However, this has not been demonstrated at the single cell level.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Jchain expression is not overly represented in IgA or IgM expressing PCs compared to IgG1+ PCs.
source: Taken together, these data suggested that Jchain expression is not overly represented in IgA or IgM expressing PCs compared to IgG1+ PCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on isotype distribution.

claim: JchaincreERT2 mediated cre-loxP recombination occurs across immunoglobulin isotypes.
source: We concluded that JchaincreERT2 mediated cre-loxP recombination occurs across immunoglobulin isotypes and thus that the JchaincreERT2 allele is a useful tool for genetic manipulation also of IgG1 expressing PCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on isotype distribution.

claim: It is currently accepted that a fraction of PCs in the mouse survives for periods longer than 3 months.
source: These studies have provided fundamental insights on PC maintenance and currently it is accepted that a fraction of PCs in the mouse survives for periods longer than 3 months (Ho et al., 1986; Lemke et al., 2016; Manz et al., 1998; Manz et al., 1997; Slifka et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as current understanding with citations.

claim: Nucleotide analog methodology requires cell division and is not appropriate to study global population turnover in tissues given the quiescent nature of PCs.
source: However, given the quiescent nature of PCs and that nucleotide analog methodology requires cell division, these methods are not appropriate to study global population turnover in tissues.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of nucleotide analog methodology.

claim: Over a period of 5 months the cell number of total and GFP+ PCs remained constant over time in spleen and bone marrow.
source: We found that over a period of 5 months the cell number of total and GFP+ PCs remained constant over time (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is based on longitudinal analysis shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The cell number of GFP+RFP+ cells decayed in both the spleen (t1/2 ~31.63d) and bone marrow (t1/2 ~251.93d).
source: By contrast, the cell number of GFP+RFP+ cells decayed (Figure 6B,C) in both the spleen (t1/2 ~31.63d) and bone marrow (t1/2 ~251.93d; Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is based on longitudinal analysis shown in Figure 6B,C,D,E.

claim: The half-life of PC residence differs between spleen and the bone marrow.
source: These results may agree with the knowledge that the half-life of PC residence differs between spleen and the bone marrow (Sze et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: The emergence of GFP+RFPneg cells paralleled the decay in cell numbers of GFP+RFP+ cells both in the spleen (t1/2 ~20.20d) and bone marrow (t1/2 ~190.19d).
source: Notably, analysis of the GFP+RFPneg cell numbers revealed that the emergence of these cells paralleled that observed for the decay in cell numbers of GFP+RFP+ cells (Figure 6B,C) both in the spleen (t1/2 ~20.20d) and bone marrow (t1/2 ~190.19d; Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is based on longitudinal analysis shown in Figure 6B,C,F,G.

claim: The turnover of the PC population is homeostatically regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
source: These data indicated that the turnover of the PC population is homeostatically regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the longitudinal experimental data.

claim: Homeostatic control of mature B cell numbers is widely accepted.
source: Homeostatic control of mature B cell numbers is widely accepted (Crowley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: In mature B cells, the expression of a B cell receptor is crucial for cell survival.
source: In mature B cells, the expression of a B cell receptor is crucial for cell survival (Srinivasan et al., 2009; however, BAFF is the limited resource that defines the boundaries of the biological 'space'; Crowley et al., 2009; Srinivasan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: BAFF is the limited resource that defines the boundaries of the biological 'space' for mature B cells.
source: In mature B cells, the expression of a B cell receptor is crucial for cell survival (Srinivasan et al., 2009; however, BAFF is the limited resource that defines the boundaries of the biological 'space'; Crowley et al., 2009; Srinivasan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: PCs express the BCMA receptor that allows the sensing of both BAFF and APRIL.
source: PCs express the BCMA receptor that allows the sensing of both BAFF and APRIL, and BCMA deficient mice have reduced PC numbers (O'Connor et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: BCMA deficient mice have reduced PC numbers.
source: PCs express the BCMA receptor that allows the sensing of both BAFF and APRIL, and BCMA deficient mice have reduced PC numbers (O'Connor et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: BCMA is expressed in B cells committed to PC differentiation.
source: However, because BCMA is expressed in B cells committed to PC differentiation further studies are required to disentangle formation and maintenance (Mackay et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation.

claim: PC homeostatic regulation could be the reflection of a limited number of niches in a given organ which would then limit the number of PCs.
source: PC homeostatic regulation could also be the reflection of a limited number of niches in a given organ which would then limit the number of PCs (Höfer et al., 2006; Khodadadi et al., 2019; Lightman et al., 2019; Lindquist et al., 2019; Wilmore and Allman, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis with citations.

claim: The JchaincreERT2 allele is a validated PC specific genetic tool that paves the way for an in-depth mechanistic understanding of PC biology and pathology in vivo, in their microenvironment.
source: The JchaincreERT2 is thus a validated PC specific genetic tool that paves the way for an in-depth mechanistic understanding of PC biology and pathology in vivo, in their microenvironment.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Genetic manipulation of PCs has been available for B cells since 1997.
source: One underlying cause is the lack of tools for specific genetic manipulation of PCs, something available for B cells since 1997, more than 20 years ago (Rickert et al., 1997), and more recently for B cells at multiple stages of development (Boross et al., 2009; Casola et al., 2006; Croker et al., 2004; Crouch et al., 2007; de Boer et al., 2003; Dogan et al., 2009; Düber et al., 2009; Georgiades et al., 2002; Hobeika et al., 2006; Kraus et al., 2004; Kwon et al., 2008; Moriyama et al., 2014; Robbiani et al., 2008; Schweighoffer et al., 2013; Shinnakasu et al., 2016; Weber et al., 2019; Yasuda et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as historical context with citations.

claim: The initiation of Jchain expression does not require BLIMP1.
source: This data agrees with previous work using in vitro cultures of Blimp1 deficient B cells suggesting that the initiation of Jchain expression does not require BLIMP1 (Kallies et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as agreement with previous work with a citation.

claim: In the JchaincreERT2 allele GFP and creERT2 are linked by a self-cleaving 2A peptide that ensures a near equitable co-expression of the proteins.
source: In the JchaincreERT2 allele GFP and creERT2 are linked by a self-cleaving 2A peptide that ensures a near equitable co-expression of the proteins (Szymczak et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a design feature with a citation.

claim: The effectiveness of cre recombination likely correlates with the level of creERT2 expression because PCs expressed the highest level of Jchain.
source: As consequence, it is likely that the effectiveness of cre recombination correlates with the level of creERT2 expression because PCs expressed the highest level of Jchain, as suggested by GFP expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the design and expression data.

claim: The JchaincreERT2 allele analyzed in this work retained the puromycin selection cassette that is flanked by rox recombination sites.
source: Of note, the JchaincreERT2 allele analyzed in this work retained the puromycin selection cassette that is flanked by rox recombination sites.
evidence: This is stated as a technical detail of the allele.

claim: Retention of the selection cassette can reduce gene expression of the targeted locus.
source: On occasion it has been observed that retention of the selection cassette reduces gene expression of the targeted locus (Meyers et al., 1998; Nagy et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as a known issue with citations.

claim: In the JchaincreERT2 allele the expression of Jchain is interrupted by a GFP-2A-creERT2 cassette and induction of cre-mediated recombination deletes Jchain exon two that is loxP-flanked.
source: Finally, in the JchaincreERT2 allele the expression of Jchain is interrupted by a GFP-2A-creERT2 cassette and induction of cre-mediated recombination deletes Jchain exon two that is loxP-flanked.
evidence: This is stated as a technical detail of the allele.

claim: Heterozygous deletion of Jchain displayed an intermediate phenotype to that of knockout mice.
source: It was previously shown that heterozygous deletion of Jchain displayed an intermediate phenotype to that of knockout mice (Lycke et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as previous knowledge with a citation.

claim: The JchaincreERT2 allele allows genetic manipulation of PCs in vivo in their microenvironment, and to retrieve live time-stamped PCs for downstream analysis.
source: The JchaincreERT2 allele is highly suited to perform these investigations as it allows genetic manipulation of PCs in vivo in their microenvironment, and to retrieve live time-stamped PCs for downstream analysis.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the tool.
